name: Subbrow excision

lead: Subbrow excision removes a strip of skin along the lower edge of the eyebrow, lifting a low brow and the lateral upper-lid hooding beneath it.

It helps looks by opening the eye area and reducing heavy-lidded appearance. Case series report high satisfaction: in a 2025 study of 33 patients, 75.7% reported significant or considerable improvement.

paras: A surgeon marks and removes excess skin in the brow line, sometimes adding muscle work, and closes the incision. Results are assessed over months.
Reported effects include temporary redness and swelling and a scar hidden in the brow. Wikipedia notes direct brow lifts most often cause numbness among lift types.

angle.text: The incision at the lower brow edge lifts the brow and trims excess lateral lid skin, changing eye shape and brow position.

lead: Subbrow excision is a surgical procedure in which skin is removed under the eyebrow to lift the brow and reduce upper-lid skin fold.[1][2] It is used for brow ptosis and lateral hooding.[2]

Surgeons describe variants. One 2020 series of 564 patients attached the orbicularis oculi muscle to the frontalis to improve durability.[1] Another technique divides forehead depressor muscles through the same incision to treat brow ptosis and glabellar lines.[3]

paras: In the 564-patient series, average excision size was 55 mm by 8 mm and the muscle was anchored to the frontalis.[1] Another approach avulses depressor muscles and fixes the brow to periosteum when needed.[3]
Of 33 patients aged 47 to 71 followed six months, 25 (75.7%) reported significant or considerable improvement; complications were mostly temporary swelling and redness, with rare evident scarring.[2]
Studies are case series and cohorts rather than randomized trials.[1][2]
